title: IEEE -0.0 and +0.0 compare equal, but SIGN(1.0, -0.0) returns -1.0
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE COPY_SIGN(MAGN, FROM, OUT)
C     SIGN(A, B) returns ABS(A) with the sign of B. The trap: B can
C     be -0.0, in which case SIGN(1.0, -0.0) = -1.0 even though
C     -0.0 .EQ. 0.0 is .TRUE. A naive port via Math.copySign or
C     SIGN(A) * ABS(B) needs to preserve the negative-zero sign
C     bit, not the value.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL MAGN, FROM, OUT
      OUT = SIGN(MAGN, FROM)
      RETURN
      END
notes: SIGN's negative-zero handling is a known port hazard. The Java equivalent is Math.copySign(MAGN, FROM). The naive 'if FROM < 0 negate' breaks for -0.0 because FROM < 0 is false. Capture the IEEE sign-bit semantic explicitly.
